clue.text: Will's lady has project involving story

definitions.note: Will is William Shakespeare; one of his heroines is the lover of Romeo

indicators.note: involving means the word for project wraps around the word for story

parts.note: to project is to stick out, to jut
a story can be a falsehood, a lie

explanation.surface: A woman named in a will is backing a venture with a tale attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a legal document, but it is Shakespeare's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The heroine of Romeo and Juliet is a leading lady created by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Period when Julius Caesar captures Russia in revolt

indicators.note: captures means the initials take the shuffled country into custody between them

parts.note: the initials of Julius Caesar are J and C

indicators.note: a country in revolt is overturned, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A historical moment when Rome's dictator seizes a rebellious Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolt' is the anagram signal, and 'captures' puts the result between the dictator's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: The geological time between the Triassic and Cretaceous is a named era of dinosaurs.

clue.text: Wantonly sins with zeal — not with this sin!

indicators.note: wantonly means recklessly and without restraint, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A wry remark that someone sinning eagerly can at least not be accused of idleness.
explanation.walkthrough: Sloth is one of the seven deadly sins, and sinning with zeal is the opposite of it, so the clue's last part also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth, idleness, is listed among the seven deadly sins, so it is a sin.

clue.text: Make bread

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so making bread is being paid for work rather than baking

explanation.surface: A baker's instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The baker's reading is the false one; bread is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money from work is to be paid a wage or salary.

clue.text: Maybe captain's lip to bowler?

parts.note: lip is cheek or insolence, as is brass (brass neck)
a bowler is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A cricket team's captain giving cheek to the bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture misleads: the bowler is a hat, and the captain is a military officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Senior military officers wore gold braid on their caps, giving a slang name for high-ranking officers such as a captain.

clue.text: Memorial soldiers found in playground

indicators.note: found in means the soldiers are discovered inside the playground

parts.note: a rec (recreation ground) is a British term for a public playground or park
LI stands for Light Infantry

explanation.surface: A war memorial to soldiers located in a public park.
explanation.definitionFit: Something surviving from the past serves as a reminder or keepsake of it.

clue.text: Harshly criticise second strike

parts.note: to lam is to hit or thrash

explanation.surface: A critic attacking a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial verb for attacking fiercely in words, as a reviewer might pan a play.

clue.text: Sailors in house next to toy maker

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
by means beside, next to

explanation.surface: Sailors living in a house beside a toy factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Hornby is a British maker of model railways and toy trains.
explanation.definitionFit: The British firm famous for model trains and Meccano is a manufacturer of toys.

clue.text: Finish off Sanctus composed in Italian

indicators.note: composed means put together afresh, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to finish off here is to cut off the final letter of the word Sanctus

explanation.surface: A musical instruction to complete a Mass setting written in Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish off' removes the last S of SANCTUS, and 'composed' rearranges SANCTU.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Tuscany, the region around Florence, is an Italian.

clue.text: Republican islands losing base in cuts

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the islands' name

parts.note: the Azores are an Atlantic island group
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A Republican government's budget cuts hurting its Atlantic islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The political reading misleads; 'cuts' is a verb, shaves with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to shave or slice with a sharp blade.

clue.text: Large bird sadly swallows pet rook

indicators.note: swallows means the word for sadly takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sadness
a cat is a pet
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A big bird mournfully gulping down someone's pet crow.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for a large seabird such as the frigate bird or pelican.

clue.text: Women intimate with film producer

parts.note: inner means private, intimate (inner thoughts)

explanation.surface: A movie mogul getting close to women.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Winner was a British film director and producer, known for Death Wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Winner produced and directed films, so the surname names a film producer.

clue.text: Call some prison guards

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Summon some of the prison officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's call is its song, the sound it makes.

clue.text: Put up with sales talk

definitions.meaning: to put up a tent is to erect it

explanation.surface: Tolerating a salesperson's patter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' reads as tolerate, but 'with' only links the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: erecting a tent, and a sales spiel.

clue.text: Either way he's Jesus' father

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: the Aramaic word for father, which Jesus used of God

explanation.surface: A statement about the parentage of Jesus.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for father in Jesus' Aramaic is a palindrome, so the definition does double duty; it is also the name of the Swedish pop group.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels Jesus addresses God with the Aramaic word for father.

clue.text: Excitement of month in Mali after leaving Indonesia

indicators.note: after leaving means the country's code has departed from the month

parts.note: French is spoken in Mali, and the French for February is fevrier
RI is the international vehicle code for Indonesia

explanation.surface: A traveller's thrill at a month in Mali after leaving Indonesia.
explanation.walkthrough: Mali's official language was French, so its February is FEVRIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous agitation or excited enthusiasm, as in election fever.

clue.text: Odd joke

explanation.surface: A strange gag.
explanation.definitionFit: It means peculiar, and as a noun a quip that raises a laugh.

clue.text: Internal security has to prosecute children

parts.note: IS is the abbreviation for internal security
to sue is to take legal action against

explanation.surface: State security has to take parents' offspring to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring are a person's issue, a legal and literary term for descendants.

clue.text: Rain cloud cut short play after game

indicators.note: after places the shortened play behind the game

parts.note: nim is a game of taking objects from heaps

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: to busk is to play music in the street

explanation.surface: Rain stops play early after a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the K from BUSK, leaving BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteorologists use the term for a grey rain-bearing cloud layer.

clue.text: Could two males lead to havoc?

parts.note: may and could both express possibility
HE is a male pronoun and M the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A question about whether two men together cause chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos and wild disorder; havoc is a close synonym.

clue.text: Drunken vintner welcoming daughter's convenience food

indicators.note: welcoming means the jumbled letters take the daughter inside
a drunken person staggers about, so the letters of vintner are jumbled

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A drunk wine merchant welcomes his daughter's ready meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' is the anagram signal and 'welcoming' puts the daughter inside the result; the wine merchant is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-packaged ready meal eaten in front of the television is a quick convenience food.

clue.text: Recoils after surreptitious rugby manoeuvres

indicators.note: after says the recoils come behind the surreptitious word

parts.note: fly means sly, cunning
a gun kicks when it recoils

explanation.surface: Sneaky rugby tactics followed by a backlash.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby, kicking a loose ball along the ground is a recognised move, a type of kick.

clue.text: Show signs of non-atomic form of radiation

indicators.note: non- says the atomic letter is not wanted

parts.note: beta rays are a type of radiation
A stands for atomic, as in A-bomb

explanation.surface: Showing symptoms of non-nuclear radiation exposure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-' drops one A from BETA RAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal unintentionally, as in a face that gives away nerves.

clue.text: Book of Leviticus about to be reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed is read as re-viewed, looked at backwards, so the letters turn round

parts.note: Lev is the abbreviation for Leviticus
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A Bible book about to be assessed by a critic.
explanation.definitionFit: A long work of fiction published as a volume.

clue.text: Be quiet and run away with Indian banker

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
off means away, departed

explanation.surface: Advice to absconding with money from an Indian bank.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Asia the word names a money-changer or banker.

clue.text: Concluded a good wine includes hint of earthiness

indicators.note: includes means the wine takes the hint inside it

parts.note: red is wine

indicators.note: a hint of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wine tasting verdict about an earthy note.
explanation.definitionFit: Came to a settled decision; agreed and concluded both mean decided.

clue.text: Angry drunk advanced

explanation.surface: An aggressive tipsy person moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: intense in feeling, intoxicated, and elevated or advanced.

clue.text: Helpless rector departs in a huff

indicators.note: departs means the rector leaves the word

parts.note: narked is British slang for annoyed

explanation.surface: A rector storms out in a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprotected and defenceless, as in naked aggression or vulnerable.

clue.text: Dealer in Volkswagen trucks

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A car salesman for Volkswagen lorries.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative who deals on behalf of others, as a sales agent.

clue.text: Take a small cut

explanation.surface: Instruction to cut slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for stealing, and also a shallow notch.

clue.text: Liberal doctor raised young lass

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to doctor is to falsify or fix, to rig

explanation.surface: A liberal-minded doctor brought up a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lass is a young female, a maiden.

clue.text: Jeer King John?

parts.note: boo is a jeer
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Booing King John of England.
explanation.walkthrough: King John looks like the English monarch; John is the fourth Gospel, with a question mark marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel of John is one of the volumes of the Bible.

clue.text: Small crack in a ship

parts.note: a means one
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: A slight split in a ship's hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like a split, but it means a wisecrack.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief wisecrack or quip delivered in a single sentence.

clue.text: Cheat Canadian returning to French commune

parts.note: to cog is an old word for cheating at dice

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Can is the abbreviation for Canadian

explanation.surface: A swindling Canadian heads back to a town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The brandy is named after a town in the Charente, an administrative commune of France.

clue.text: I felt DIY training is required to get accuracy

indicators.note: training shapes and reforms, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says home improvement lessons are needed for precision work.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness to the original, as in high-fidelity sound, means exactness.

clue.text: Goes around right among some runners

indicators.note: among means the right goes in the middle of the runners

parts.note: skis are runners for snow

explanation.surface: Turning right while among runners in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass around the edge of something, as a road goes round a town.
